analyst_view.overall: Excelsior (13th, 14 points) host Telstar (16th, 10 points) on Saturday in a relegation six-pointer; a home win would put Excelsior seven points clear of Telstar. Excelsior under Ruben den Uil ended a run of four defeats (including 0-9 at Twente) with a 3-2 win at Feyenoord on 21 November, their first league win in De Kuip since 1980, with on-loan winger Aymen Sliti outstanding and Widell heading the winner from a corner. Telstar lost 1-3 at home to PEC Zwolle the same night after defensive errors, though coach Henk Brugge said they were the better side on the ball; Nokkvi Thorisson was not fully fit and started on the bench. The numbers still count Gerald Alders and Rui Mendes as out for Telstar, but the latest Eredivisie injury list has neither of them, only forward Jelani Seedorf (about a 25% chance to play), and Excelsior have no injuries listed with Nesto Groen back from a ban. Danny Makkelie referees, as the numbers already assume (about 2.5 cards a game); news for this match was thin, with no full preview found two days out.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals and already add Telstar's 14 goals and Excelsior's 22 conceded in their last six. They also add about +6% to Excelsior for Gerald Alders being out and take about 3.5% off Telstar for Rui Mendes, but neither is on the latest injury list, so both look available. Undoing those two nets out to a hair lower, so I move it 1%, to about 3.37.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners and already trim Excelsior's share for their few corners lately (19 in six). Excelsior did score the winner at Feyenoord from a corner and defended deep for the last 20 minutes there, but at home against a fellow struggler they should have more of the ball; nothing on tactics or line-ups points clearly either way, so I stay at about 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.4 cards and already take about 12% off for Danny Makkelie, who books about 2.5 per game, and a little off Telstar for fewer cards lately. This is a six-pointer between two teams in the bottom five and the numbers carry no stakes adjustment for it, so I lean mildly higher, to about 2.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots and already move Excelsior down (-12.5%) and Telstar up (+9.9%) for recent form. Excelsior's win at Feyenoord showed life in their attack with Sliti in form, while Telstar had plenty of long-range efforts against PEC; with Mendes and Alders apparently fit and Seedorf, out for two weeks already, still doubtful, these roughly balance, so I stay at about 26.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target and already count Excelsior's poor accuracy lately (12 on target in six) and Telstar's better run (37). PEC's keeper saved all of Telstar's long shots last week, which fits that pattern; nothing new on either attack beyond what the form figures show, so I stay at about 9.9.
